When a current of 5 mA is passed through a galvanometer having a coil of resistance 15<mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="SVG" overflow="overflow"><svg style="vertical-align: 0;" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="1.633ex" height="1.593ex" role="img" focusable="false" viewBox="0 -704 722 704" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><g stroke="currentColor" fill="currentColor" stroke-width="0" transform="scale(1,-1)"><g data-mml-node="math"><g data-mml-node="mi"><use data-c="3A9" xlink:href="#MJX-TEX-N-3A9"></use></g></g></g></svg></mjx-container>, it shows full
scale deflection. The value of the resistance to be put in series with the galvanometer to convert it into a
voltmeter of range 0 – 10V is:

2.045 × 10<sup>3</sup> <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="SVG" overflow="overflow"><svg style="vertical-align: 0;" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="1.633ex" height="1.593ex" role="img" focusable="false" viewBox="0 -704 722 704" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><g stroke="currentColor" fill="currentColor" stroke-width="0" transform="scale(1,-1)"><g data-mml-node="math"><g data-mml-node="mi"><use data-c="3A9" xlink:href="#MJX-TEX-N-3A9"></use></g></g></g></svg></mjx-container>

explanation:
Given : Current through the galvanometer,

ig = 5 × 10–3 A

Galvanometer resistance, G = 15

Let resistance R to be put in series with the galvanometer to convert it into a voltmeter.

V = ig (R + G)

10 = 5 × 10–3 (R + 15)

R = 2000 – 15 = 1985

= 1.985 × 103
